listings.name: The Boatslip Resort & Beach Club
listings.description: A waterfront resort in the West End, and home of Tea Dance, the late-afternoon party on the deck that has run since the late 1960s. The Buoy Bar is on site.

listings.name: Perry's Fine Wine & Liquors
listings.description: A wine and liquor shop open since 1934, also selling food and gifts, which delivers across the Outer Cape.

history.event: Perry's opens.

listings.name: Provincetown United Methodist Church
listings.description: A Methodist congregation on Shank Painter Road, with Sunday service at 10 a.m., also carried on 107.7 FM and online.

listings.name: Pilgrim Monument & Provincetown Museum
listings.opening_hours_raw: Apr 1-May Mo [-1] 09:00-17:00;May Mo [-1] - Sep Mo [1] 09:00-19:00;Sep Mo [1] - Nov 30 09:00-17:00;Nov Th[4] off;Dec-Mar off

photos.what: Pilgrim Monument and Bas Relief as viewed from Bradford St.

amenities: Climb to the top (116 steps and 60 ramps)
Last ticket 3 p.m.; last climb 3:15 p.m.
listings.description: The granite tower on High Pole Hill that you can see from almost anywhere on the Outer Cape. At 252 feet it is the tallest all-granite structure in the United States, modelled on the Torre del Mangia in Siena, and it marks the Pilgrims' first landfall in 1620 and the signing of the Mayflower Compact in Provincetown Harbor. Visitors climb 116 steps and 60 ramps to the top; the Provincetown Museum at its base tells the town's maritime story.

history.event: The Mayflower anchors in Provincetown Harbor; the Mayflower Compact is signed aboard.
President Theodore Roosevelt lays the cornerstone on August 20.
President William H. Taft dedicates the finished monument on August 5.

listings.name: Gifford House
listings.description: A historic inn a block off Commercial Street that doubles as an entertainment complex, with the Porch Bar, a lounge with a grand piano, and the Club Purgatory dance club downstairs. No breakfast is served (coffee, tea and fruit are set out in the lounge mornings) and pets are not allowed.

listings.name: Gaslamp Bed & Breakfast
listings.description: A gay-owned, adults-only (18+) bed and breakfast in a renovated late-1800s Victorian, with seven rooms (four with gas fireplaces). Breakfast is included, and there is a year-round hot tub and a clothing-optional deck garden.

listings.name: Waterford Inn Provincetown
listings.description: A small historic inn on Commercial Street in the East End, updated as a boutique hotel.

listings.name: Anchor Inn Beach House
listings.description: A waterfront inn on the harbor at the start of the West End, with rooms looking out over Provincetown Harbor.

listings.name: Somerset House Inn
listings.description: A woman-owned guesthouse in a historic house on Commercial Street, open year-round, with complimentary breakfast and evening beer-and-wine receptions.

listings.name: Provincetown Inn
listings.description: A historic waterfront resort at the far West End where Commercial Street begins, with a large outdoor waterfront pool, the West End Lounge, a pool bar and the Breakwater Cafe. Pets are accepted in designated rooms for a fee.

listings.name: Harbor Hotel Provincetown
listings.description: A waterfront hotel at the East End with a heated outdoor pool, the Cabana Bar & Grill, fire pits, and pet-friendly rooms (fee). A complimentary shuttle runs into town in season.

listings.name: Cape Codder Guest House
listings.description: A beachfront guesthouse in the East End, with a private beach and views over the bay.

listings.name: Surfside Hotel & Suites
listings.description: An East End waterfront hotel with a private beach on the bay, an outdoor pool with the Lighthouse Bar, and suites with kitchens. Continental breakfast is included, and it is pet-friendly.

listings.name: Berta Walker Gallery
listings.description: A gallery showing the history of American art through Provincetown's artists, from the art colony's founders to painters working today.

listings.name: Provincetown Art Association & Museum (PAAM)

photos.what: Entrance to the Provincetown Art Association and Museum.

listings.description: Founded in 1914 by the artists of what is now the oldest continuous art colony in America, PAAM shows work by Provincetown artists past and present in five galleries. The shows run from traditional Cape Cod landscape to new contemporary work, and they change through the year alongside the permanent collection.

history.event: Founded by the artists of the Provincetown art colony.
Centennial.

listings.name: The Benchmark
listings.description: An adults-only inn, now run together with its neighbor, 8 Dyer Hotel.

listings.name: 8 Dyer Hotel
listings.description: An adults-only small hotel on Dyer Street, now run together with its neighbor, the Benchmark Inn.

listings.name: Admiral's Landing
listings.description: A historic 1860s inn at the corner of Bradford and Pearl, a block from Commercial Street and the bay.

listings.name: White Porch Inn
listings.description: An art-focused boutique inn on Johnson Street, close to the beaches, galleries and restaurants.

listings.name: Salt House Inn
listings.description: A small, modern bed & breakfast in the center of town, known for its breakfasts.

listings.name: Sunset Inn
listings.description: One of Provincetown's oldest guesthouses: a mid-nineteenth-century house that has taken in visitors for more than fifty years.

listings.name: Crowne Pointe Historic Inn & Spa
listings.description: An adults-only (18+) historic inn on Bradford Street with a saltwater pool and the Shui Spa (soaking tub, steam room, salt sauna). Breakfast is included, and one dog per room is accepted for a nightly fee.

listings.name: Brass Key Guesthouse
listings.description: An adults-only (21+) guesthouse spread over nine restored historic buildings, with an infinity pool, a large spa tub, and a hot breakfast daily. Dogs are accepted in select rooms with advance notice. Seasonal.

listings.name: Rose & Crown Guest House
listings.description: A historic guesthouse in the center of town on Commercial Street.

listings.name: Mercury Hotel
listings.description: A boutique hotel on Winthrop Street near the beach, in walking distance of Commercial Street.

listings.name: The Bradford
listings.description: Quiet lodging on Bradford Street, a few steps from the shops, restaurants and harbor beaches.

listings.name: Red Inn
amenities: Happy hour Fri–Sun 2–4:30; raw-bar happy hour daily 2–4:30
listings.description: The restaurant of a West End waterfront inn, with views across the harbor to Long Point. Serves dinner nightly, a raw-bar happy hour, and a jazz brunch on Sundays.

listings.name: Seaglass Inn & Spa
listings.description: An LGBTQ+- and family-friendly boutique hotel on four acres in the West End, with a pool, a seasonal bar and a spa.

listings.name: Cape Colony Inn
listings.description: An LGBTQ+-friendly hotel two blocks from the beach on upper Bradford Street, with a heated outdoor pool, fire pit and grills. Pets are allowed, and parking and Wi-Fi are free.

listings.name: AWOL
listings.description: A 30-room boutique hotel by the Province Lands moors, about a mile and a half from the town center, run by Lark Hotels. It has a heated pool and fire pits, and takes up to two dogs per room (70 lb or less) for a fee. Seasonal (formerly the Inn at the Moors).

listings.name: Provincetown Town Hall
listings.description: The town's seat of government, dedicated in 1886: a Romanesque and Queen Anne building with a clock tower at the center of Commercial Street. Upstairs, its auditorium has been a roller rink, a basketball court and a dance hall, and it still hosts town meeting and performances. A restoration of more than $6 million was finished in 2010.

history.event: Dedicated on August 25, after construction began in September 1885 at a cost of $50,400.
A two-year restoration of more than $6 million is largely completed in November.

listings.name: Unitarian Universalist Meeting House of Provincetown

photos.what: the First Universalist Church in Provincetown today

listings.description: A white meeting house on Commercial Street where the Unitarian Universalist congregation meets for Sunday service at 11 a.m. (also streamed). During the week it hosts concerts, including Great Music Provincetown, and community meetings.

history.event: The Universalist congregation is established in Provincetown.
The present meeting house, designed by Benjamin Hallett, is built; the steeple was added later.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places as the First Universalist Church.
Included in the Provincetown Historic District.

listings.name: The Canteen
listings.description: A casual spot in the center of town for seasonal food, with dog-friendly seating outside, a raw bar, and a beach bar out back. Open year-round.

listings.name: Saint Peter the Apostle Church
listings.description: The Roman Catholic parish church of Provincetown and Truro, founded in 1874 largely by the town's Portuguese fishing families. The original wooden church burned in 2005, and the present church, keeping one surviving stained-glass window, was dedicated in 2008. Each June the Blessing of the Fleet procession sets out from here to MacMillan Wharf during the Portuguese Festival.

history.event: The first St. Peter's church is dedicated in October; most parishioners are Portuguese fishing families.
Provincetown's Blessing of the Fleet begins, with a procession from St. Peter's to the wharf.
The original church is destroyed by fire in January; one stained-glass window is saved.
The new church is dedicated in July.

listings.name: The Mews Restaurant & Café
listings.description: A long-running restaurant with two floors on the beach: an upstairs bistro and a quieter beach-level dining room, serving the same menu.

listings.name: Church of St. Mary of the Harbor
listings.description: The Episcopal church in the East End, on the water. Services are Sunday at 10 a.m. and Saturday at 8:30 a.m., and it is home to the East End Music concert series.

history.event: A group of Episcopalians raises $2,500 to buy an old house on the harbor and turn it into a church.
The mission calls the Rev. Robert Wood Nicholson as its first vicar; under him local artists furnish and decorate the church.

listings.name: Fine Arts Work Center

photos.what: Fine Arts Work Center's outdoor seating area.

listings.description: A nonprofit residency for emerging visual artists and writers. It is best known for its seven-month winter fellowships, which bring twenty early-career artists and writers to live and work in Provincetown, and for keeping the art colony going year-round.

history.event: Frank A. Days builds artist studios above the lumber bins of his Pearl Street yard; Ross Moffett is among the first tenants.
The Fine Arts Work Center is founded, first based at 135 Bradford Street.
The Center buys the Pearl Street lumberyard property.
First major reconstruction; the coal shed becomes the Stanley Kunitz Common Room.
Reconstruction of the historic studios building is completed (work 2009-2010).

listings.name: Cape Cod 5
listings.description: The Provincetown branch of a community bank serving Cape Cod, the Islands and southeastern Massachusetts.

listings.name: Veterans Memorial Community Center
listings.description: A town-run community center in the former Veterans Memorial Elementary School, housing the Council on Aging, Recreation and Human Services departments along with meeting rooms, a gym and early-childhood programs. It serves as a multigenerational hub for classes, senior services and public meetings.

history.event: Veterans Memorial Elementary School, designed by Walter M. Gaffney of Hyannis, opens.
The elementary school closes; Town Meeting votes to move the Council on Aging, Human Services, Recreation and DPW offices into the building as the Veterans Memorial Community Center.
In July the Council on Aging joins the school's infant-and-toddler program at the center, creating a multigenerational activity center.

listings.name: Mac's Fish House
amenities: Outdoor beach bar with fire pit
listings.description: A seafood restaurant and market from the Mac's family, which began with a fish market on the Wellfleet pier in 1995 and still buys much of its catch from local fishing families.

listings.name: Stop & Shop
listings.description: The town's full-size supermarket, on Shank Painter Road away from Commercial Street, with a deli, an in-store pharmacy and a gas station.

listings.name: Womencrafts
listings.description: A lesbian-owned and -operated feminist book and gift shop, open since 1976 and long a gathering point for activism and community in town.

history.event: Womencrafts opens.

listings.name: Shor Home
listings.description: A home furnishings shop with an interior design studio.

listings.name: Ptown Bikes
listings.description: Provincetown's bike shop since 1995, renting and selling Trek, Specialized and Electra bikes and doing repairs.

listings.name: Provincetown Theater
listings.description: A nonprofit performing-arts venue on Bradford Street that has produced new work and contemporary American theater since 2001, with a full season of shows through the year.

listings.name: The Pointe Tavern
listings.description: The restaurant and wine bar of the Crowne Pointe Hotel & Spa, serving breakfast and a modern coastal American dinner menu with cocktails and wine; the room looks toward the Pilgrim Monument.

listings.name: Toys of Eros
listings.description: An adult shop that doubles as a small free museum of the history of sex toys, from ancient artifacts and reproductions to modern devices. Opened in 1996; its staff are trained as sex educators. Explicit content — adults only in practice.

listings.name: Far Land Provisions
listings.description: A corner store and deli with its own bakery, prepared foods, and breakfast and lunch sandwiches made to order.

listings.name: Ace Conwell Home Center
listings.description: The town's Ace Hardware, lumber yard and Benjamin Moore paint store, with garden, grill and tool departments.

listings.name: Yolqueria
listings.description: Brunch and tacos served on a breezy porch or indoors, all season.

listings.name: Victor's
listings.description: A West End restaurant in a cottage-style building with a cathedral ceiling and stone fireplace, serving New American small plates meant for sharing.

listings.name: Tin Pan Alley
listings.description: A restaurant and live piano bar serving seasonal New American food with global touches, with breads, sauces and desserts made in-house.

listings.name: The Provincetown Bookshop
listings.description: The oldest bookstore on Cape Cod, open since 1932, with LGBTQ+ titles, cookbooks, children's books, art and design, vinyl and a bargain table.

history.event: The Provincetown Bookshop opens.

listings.name: The Mayflower
listings.description: A casual American restaurant on Commercial Street with a long, reasonably priced menu. Brothers Mike and Sam Janoplis opened it in 1929, and it has stayed in the family ever since.

history.event: Mike and Sam Janoplis open the Mayflower.

listings.name: Post Office Cafe & Cabaret
listings.description: A Commercial Street standby for close to fifty years, with breakfast and an all-day American menu, two bars, and live cabaret most nights. The building was a marine-supply store in 1940 and the Wreck Club from 1960.

history.event: Lands End Marine Supply opens in the building.
Converted into the Wreck Club.

listings.name: Cabot's Candy
listings.description: A family-run candy maker that has pulled salt water taffy since 1927. It also sells fudge, brittle and bulk candy.

history.event: Cabot's begins making salt water taffy.

listings.name: The Penney Patch
listings.description: A candy shop on Commercial Street selling homemade fudge and salt water taffy, with bulk candy and chocolates for gifts.

listings.name: Provincetown Community Television
listings.description: The town's community-access television station. It carries live and archived coverage of Provincetown government meetings alongside locally made programs.

listings.name: East End Market
listings.description: An East End neighborhood market on Bradford Street selling groceries and produce, prepared breakfast and lunch, and wine, beer and spirits.

listings.name: Summer of SASS
listings.description: Nonprofit founded by comedian Kristen Becker that brings LGBTQ+ young adults (18–20) from unwelcoming places to spend a summer in Provincetown, with subsidized travel, starter housing, job connections and mentoring. Participants live at 210 Bradford Street (the Stowaway Guest House).

listings.name: Bubala's by the Bay
listings.description: A restaurant serving lunch, dinner and cocktails daily on Commercial Street; dinner reservations are taken for groups of five or more.

listings.name: The Ellery Hotel
listings.description: A boutique hotel on Johnson Street, a short walk from Commercial Street.

listings.name: Provincetown Dental Arts (Scott A. Allegretti, DDS)
listings.opening_hours_raw: Mo off; Tu-Fr 09:00-17:00; Sa "by appointment"; Su off
listings.description: General and cosmetic dental practice of Dr. Scott A. Allegretti on Bradford Street, offering cleanings, fillings, whitening, implants and veneers.

listings.name: Shipwreck Lounge at the Brass Key
listings.description: The cocktail lounge of the Brass Key Guesthouse, open to the public, with a large fireplace, wood interiors and handcrafted cocktails.

listings.name: Porch Bar at Gifford House
listings.description: The bar of the Gifford House inn, an LGBTQ+ lounge with indoor seating by a fireplace, a pool table and an outdoor porch, serving cocktails, beer and wine. Open all year.

listings.name: Kohi Coffee
listings.description: A coffee bar serving espresso and pour-overs.

listings.name: 1620 Brewhouse
listings.description: A pub and alehouse with 12 draft taps, pub-classic food and live entertainment.

listings.name: Vorelli's
listings.description: A casual restaurant and bar serving burgers, Wellfleet oysters, stuffed clams, deli sandwiches, salads and lobster rolls, and known for its Bloody Marys.

listings.name: Waters Edge Cinema
listings.description: A year-round two-screen movie theater on the second floor of Whaler's Wharf, run by the nonprofit Provincetown Film Society (which also stages the Provincetown International Film Festival). Shows new releases, mini-festivals and guest presentations.

history.event: Provincetown Film Society buys and renovates the Whaler's Wharf Cinema, reopening it as Waters Edge Cinema

listings.name: Adam's Variety
listings.description: A variety store on the site of the former Adam's Pharmacy, selling beach and everyday essentials, health and beauty items, snacks, souvenirs, hardware basics, cards, lottery, tobacco and vape products. It stopped being a pharmacy and was rebranded after a 2024 ownership change.

listings.name: Pepe's Wharf
listings.description: A two-story restaurant on the harbor side of Commercial Street, with two decks over the water and dining inside and out.

listings.name: Adam's Nest
listings.description: A queer-owned shop of activist apparel, art, jewelry and books. Ten percent of every cause piece goes back to LGBTQ+ organizations.

listings.name: Coffey Men
listings.description: A menswear shop that makes its own small line of clothing and accessories.

listings.name: WOMR 92.1 FM
listings.description: Listener-supported community radio station broadcasting from Provincetown on 92.1 FM, with sister station WFMR 91.3 FM; volunteer DJs host a wide mix of music and talk.

listings.name: Rice Polak Gallery
listings.description: A contemporary gallery showing painting, photography and sculpture by mid-career and emerging artists.

listings.name: Simie Maryles Gallery
listings.description: A gallery of traditional painting and sculpture by contemporary artists, from the United States and abroad.

listings.name: Utilities Home
listings.description: A kitchen, bath and home shop stocking cookware and household basics from brands such as Le Creuset, Staub and Wüsthof.

listings.name: Kidstuff
listings.description: A children's specialty shop, in business for over 30 years, with clothing, gifts, books and accessories for newborns up to size 14.

listings.name: Yardarm Liquors
listings.description: A full-service liquor store off Commercial Street, family-run since 1975, with a large hand-picked wine selection plus beer and spirits; sister store to Pamet Valley Liquors in Truro. Case discounts and event delivery offered.

listings.name: Go Fish
listings.description: A Commercial Street shop selling women's clothing and accessories alongside gifts and home décor.

listings.name: Harbor Lounge
listings.description: A waterfront cocktail lounge with leather couches and wraparound windows looking over the harbor, beach and pier, serving cocktails, martinis, wine and beer. Veteran- and LGBTQIA+-owned.

listings.name: ScottCakes
listings.description: A cupcake shop that makes one kind: classic vanilla with pink buttercream, in minis, classics and gluten-free. It also ships nationwide.

listings.name: Clove & Creek
listings.description: A lifestyle shop of goods from independent makers for the home, for yourself and for outdoors. Its other shops are in Hudson and Kingston, New York.

listings.name: Patio American Grill & Cocktail Bar
listings.description: A Commercial Street grill with indoor and outdoor seating, serving local seafood (lobster dishes, a raw bar with oysters) alongside steaks, burgers, pastas and vegetarian plates, plus a cocktail bar.

listings.name: Human Rights Campaign Store
listings.description: The Human Rights Campaign's Provincetown shop, selling apparel and gifts in support of the national LGBTQ+ civil-rights organization.

listings.name: Aqua Bar
listings.description: A harborfront bar inside the Aquarium Marketplace, with a harbor-view deck and seven food vendors under the same roof. No reservations; a place to watch the sunset.

listings.name: Provincetown Business Guild
listings.description: The LGBTQ+ business association founded in 1978, with more than 300 member businesses. It markets Provincetown as a queer travel destination and produces Pride, Carnival, Holly Folly and First Light.

history.event: The Provincetown Business Guild is founded.

listings.name: B.Xclusive
listings.description: A streetwear boutique, founded in 2007, carrying vintage, made-in-USA goods, its own in-house screen-printed line, emerging brands and a large sock selection.

listings.name: Soup Kitchen in Provincetown (SKIP)
listings.description: SKIP serves a free hot lunch to Outer Cape residents on weekdays from November through April, the long off-season when the town empties out.

listings.name: Helping Our Women
listings.description: A women's health resource center for the Outer Cape, offering support for chronic illness, wellness programs and social connection.

listings.name: Hennep
listings.description: A recreational cannabis dispensary on Commercial Street. The name is Dutch for cannabis.

listings.name: Yesterday's Treasures
listings.description: A West End antiques and collectibles shop run as an LGBTQ+-owned dealers' co-op, with a changing mix of vintage finds.

listings.name: Bay Cafe
listings.description: A waterfront cafe-restaurant at the former Bayside Betsy's, now under new ownership, serving breakfast through dinner with a view over the bay.

listings.name: Local 186
listings.description: A restaurant on Commercial Street known for its burgers and fries, with the Grotta Bar on the lower level, which hosts live acts and late-night DJ parties.

listings.name: Botanica
listings.description: A gift shop and art gallery selling goods for the home and garden.

listings.name: House of La Rue
listings.description: A shop of the owners' own print designs on clothing, swimwear, accessories and home goods, in business since 2009.

listings.name: AIDS Support Group of Cape Cod — Provincetown Drop-In Center
listings.description: Provincetown drop-in center of the AIDS Support Group of Cape Cod, a Cape-wide nonprofit. It offers HIV and sexual-health services, harm reduction and Narcan training, food and nutrition help, and recovery resources.

listings.name: Provincetown Fudge Factory
listings.description: Fudge made in small batches from the same family recipe since 1984, sold with chocolates and other sweets.

history.event: Starts making fudge in Provincetown.

listings.name: Shui Spa
listings.description: Day spa at the Crowne Pointe Hotel offering massage, body treatments, energy work and facials, with a Himalayan salt sauna, steam room and hot mineral bath.

listings.name: Crown & Anchor
amenities: The Paramount — oceanside dance club (DJs, drag, theme parties)
The Wave Bar — harbor-view video bar; Showtunes on Sundays and Wednesdays
Tryst Beach Club — poolside day club (formerly listed as The Beach Club)
listings.description: A harborfront hotel and LGBTQ+ nightlife complex, now run by Tryst Hospitality, housing several bars, a dance club, a cabaret stage and a poolside day club under one roof. Tickets for shows are sold through the complex's box office and Tryst Events.

history.event: 1860s: the Central House built as a public hall, saloon and entertainment space
Expanded out over the harbor on pilings; one of the town's largest hotels
Reopened as the Crown & Anchor Motor Inn, becoming a hub of nightlife and queer culture
Destroyed by fire
Rebuilt

listings.name: Respoke
listings.description: A boutique selling footwear, clothing, accessories and furniture made from upcycled designer silk scarves.

listings.name: East End Books Ptown
listings.description: An independent bookshop in the East End, strong on LGBTQIA+ titles and art and photography books, which also runs author events.

listings.name: Bowersock Gallery
listings.description: A fine-art gallery on Commercial Street showing painting, sculpture, watercolor, photography, printmaking and assemblage by emerging, mid-career and established artists.

listings.name: Pilgrim House
listings.description: A hotel and restaurant on Commercial Street with evening entertainment, named Yankee Magazine's 2023 Editor's Choice for best Outer Cape oasis.

listings.name: Haven Center
listings.description: A recreational cannabis dispensary with shops in Provincetown and Brewster, selling flower, pre-rolls, vapes and edibles.

listings.name: Brasswood Inn
listings.description: A musician-owned bed & breakfast on Commercial Street. Each room is different, some with private balconies.

listings.name: Seamen's Bank
listings.description: Main office of Seamen's Bank, the Provincetown-headquartered community savings bank, on Commercial Street.

listings.name: Atlantic House (A-House)
listings.description: The A-House is one of the oldest continuously operating gay bars in the country, and the only gay nightclub on Cape Cod open all year. It has three bars, a dance floor with DJs, and themed nights, all in a building that has stood since 1798.

history.event: The building stands on Masonic Place.

listings.name: Provincetown Portuguese Bakery
listings.description: A long-running Portuguese bakery in the center of town, known for malasadas (fried dough) and traditional Portuguese breads and pastries. The bakery marks its 90th season in 2026.

listings.name: The Governor Bradford
listings.description: A long-running Commercial Street bar and restaurant, reopened in 2026 under new owners with a renovated room and a comfort-food menu (meatloaf, pot pie, burgers). Known for nightly drag karaoke, plus live music and sports on TV.

listings.name: The Lobster Pot
listings.description: A Provincetown seafood institution whose neon lobster sign has drawn people in off Commercial Street for generations, with harbor views from the dining room.

listings.name: On Center Gallery
listings.description: A contemporary gallery, open since 2017, specializing in painting and photography and aiming to make collecting accessible.

listings.name: Provincetown Chamber of Commerce
listings.description: The visitor welcome center at the foot of MacMillan Pier, where most ferry passengers step ashore. The Chamber has been directing travelers to Provincetown and Outer Cape lodging, dining and things to do since 1899.

history.event: John Atwood Jr. convenes leading citizens at Marine Hall to organize a Board of Trade for Provincetown.
The date the Chamber gives for its start ('Serving Provincetown's Businesses & Community Since 1897').
On January 9 the Board of Trade dissolves by unanimous vote, giving way to the Provincetown Chamber of Commerce.

listings.name: Conwell Home Center
listings.description: An Ace Hardware home center with a lumber yard, Benjamin Moore paint, a seasonal garden center, grills, pet supplies, art and office supplies, and equipment rental; it also offers screen repair and delivery.

listings.name: The Black Dog
listings.description: The Martha's Vineyard apparel and gear brand, known for its black Lab logo, in its Provincetown shop.

listings.name: Coconuts Sunglasses
listings.description: A sunglasses shop carrying Maui Jim, Ray-Ban, Oakley, Costa and other brands.

listings.name: Plush
listings.description: The Provincetown shop of Daniel Hammond's limited-edition cashmere sweaters and loungewear.

listings.name: Ptown Blooms
listings.description: A florist arranging seasonal and locally grown flowers, which also does events, weekly subscriptions and floral design classes.

listings.name: SAULT New England
listings.description: Men's, women's and kids' clothing and accessories, from a small New England chain with shops in Boston's South End and Portsmouth.

listings.name: Sniffs of Adventure
listings.description: Soy candles scented after places the two Boston owners have traveled, including Provincetown-themed scents.

listings.name: The White Hare Home & Holiday
listings.description: Home décor and holiday decorations, from glassware and decanters to Easter, Halloween and Christmas pieces.

listings.name: Ali Gray Gallery
listings.description: A contemporary art gallery with a schedule of exhibitions and gallery-stroll openings.

listings.name: Provincetown Art Gallery Association (PAGA)
listings.description: The association of Provincetown's galleries. It organizes the Friday-evening Gallery Stroll from Memorial Day weekend.

listings.name: Provincetown Arts Society
listings.description: An arts nonprofit, part of the Saint Joseph's Arts Foundation, that runs exhibitions, seasonal markets and community events.

listings.name: Flyer's Boat Rentals
listings.description: Boat rentals on the harbor in the West End.

listings.name: Center For Coastal Studies
listings.description: A marine research, rescue and education organization founded in 1976.

history.event: The Center for Coastal Studies is founded.

listings.name: Coyote Kayaks
listings.description: Kayak and paddleboard rentals and tours on the bay, plus SUP yoga and beach chair and tent rentals.

listings.name: Dolphin Fleet Whale Watch
listings.description: Whale watches from MacMillan Pier, billed as New England's first. Each trip carries a naturalist and teaches about the whales, other marine life and their habitat.

listings.name: Sanctum Paranormal
listings.description: A small museum of haunted objects and a shop, which also runs ghost tours in the evenings (Pirates & Mooncussers, and a cemetery tour).

listings.name: Sailing For All Provincetown
listings.description: A nonprofit adult sailing school that aims to make sailing affordable and open to everyone. Its home dock is at the MacMillan Pier dinghy dock.

listings.name: Aqua Bar
listings.description: A waterfront cocktail bar reached through the Aquarium Marketplace, with a deck over the harbor.

listings.name: Crown & Anchor
listings.description: A big entertainment complex in the middle of Commercial Street, with dance floors, a pool deck and a cabaret stage. It calls itself Provincetown's unofficial town square.

listings.name: Red Room
listings.description: A small performance space and bar, formerly the Velvet Lounge, staging drag, cabaret, stand-up comedy, live music and theater-festival productions; tickets are sold online per show.

listings.name: Provincetown Commons
listings.description: A shared workspace and event space for artists and other creative professionals, open to the public all year.

listings.name: Provincetown Public Library
listings.description: The town library occupies the 1860 Center Methodist Church, with its 162-foot white spire, on Commercial Street. Inside, under the vaulted ceiling, is a half-scale model of the Rose Dorothea, the Provincetown schooner that won the 1907 Lipton Cup. The model dates from the building's years as a heritage museum.

history.event: Built as the Center Methodist Church, seating 900.
Becomes the Chrysler Art Museum.
Becomes the Provincetown Heritage Museum; the half-scale Rose Dorothea is built inside from 1977.
Reopens on April 28 as the Provincetown Public Library.

listings.name: A Salted Buttery
listings.description: A breakfast-and-sandwich counter operating out of Connie's Cafe, serving breakfast sandwiches, soups and daily specials, with late-night hours for a post-bar snack.

listings.name: Grand Central
listings.description: Fresh local seafood and American dishes, served in an early-nineteenth-century ship captain's house on Masonic Place.

listings.name: Liz's Cafe
listings.description: A comfort-food breakfast and diner spot in the West End, sharing a building with Anybody's Bar. The interior was designed by Ken Fulk.

listings.name: Baedega
listings.description: A small, dimly lit cocktail lounge serving chef-driven shared plates, owned by women and LGBTQIA+ owners; it moved from Truro in March 2026 and is the first lesbian bar in town since the Pied Piper closed. About 40 seats; reservations through Resy, with limited walk-ins.

listings.name: Freemans
listings.description: An elegant coastal European restaurant in the center of town.

listings.name: Mezzeterranean
listings.description: Mediterranean small plates for dinner.

listings.name: Tin Pan Alley
listings.description: A piano bar and restaurant with live music every night, seafood and American dishes, and a patio.

listings.name: Ocean 193
listings.description: Seafood with waterfront dining, on the harbor side of Commercial Street.

listings.name: Esthetics by Evette
listings.description: A facial spa offering skincare treatments, facials and waxing.

listings.name: Provincetown Gym & Fitness
listings.description: A fitness gym on Shank Painter Road.

listings.name: Mussel Beach Health Club
listings.description: A two-floor gym of more than 8,500 square feet with free weights, cardio machines, Peloton bikes and group classes.

listings.name: Outermost Yoga
listings.description: A yoga and wellness studio with classes, retreats, beach yoga and private sessions.

listings.name: The Wellness Lab
listings.description: A med spa offering wellness and aesthetic treatments.

listings.name: The Yoga Joint
listings.description: A bright yoga studio on the bay whose four doors open onto the harbor.

listings.name: Provincetown Tennis Club
listings.description: A nonprofit, community tennis club with Har-Tru courts, lessons and clinics for every age and level.

listings.name: Coastal Acres Campground
listings.description: A seasonal campground about a ten-minute walk from Commercial Street. Open mid-April to the start of November.

listings.name: Enzo Guest House
listings.description: A guesthouse upstairs from Local 186, run by the same owners.

listings.name: The Gaslamp Bed & Breakfast
listings.description: A boutique bed & breakfast on Bradford Street.

listings.name: Guesthouse at 7 Masonic Place
listings.description: A small guesthouse in a mid-1800s building just off Commercial Street, with free parking.

listings.name: Land's End Inn
amenities: Chalice lawn bar (reopens Memorial Day weekend 2027)
listings.description: A landmark bed & breakfast at the far West End with panoramic views. It is LGBTQ-owned, adults-only (18+) and open all year. Its lawn bar, Chalice, is seasonal.

history.event: Built as a summer bungalow
Converted to a teahouse and inn
Marks 100 years of continuous operation as an inn

listings.name: The Masthead Resort & Cottages
listings.description: Cottages, suites and rooms on the harbor in the West End, with open water views. The same family has run it for more than sixty years.

listings.name: Watership Inn
listings.description: A gay-owned and -operated bed & breakfast on Winthrop Street. Continental breakfast is included.

listings.name: West End Inn
listings.description: A seven-bedroom guesthouse in a mid-1800s captain's house in the West End, run by gay men and aimed mostly at men, though all are welcome. Rooms range from a small double to a loft apartment, with a shared breakfast table.

listings.name: Angel Foods
listings.description: A full-service East End grocery with a large case of homemade prepared food, specialty aisles (Asian, Thai, Indian, Italian, Spanish) and catering all year.

listings.name: Provincetown Tourism Office
listings.description: The town's official visitor office, which publishes the official guide to Provincetown's events and activities.

history.event: Nathan Freeman builds the mansard-topped building as a gift to the town, housing the Public Library, a Y.M.C.A. and a photo studio.
The building is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Extensively renovated, with the library by then its sole occupant.
The library moves to 356 Commercial Street; the building later houses the Tourism Office and Provincetown Community Television.

listings.name: Snow & Snow
listings.description: A law firm founded by John C. Snow in 1949, described as the oldest continuously operating law firm on Cape Cod.

history.event: John C. Snow founds the firm.

listings.name: Provincetown Magazine
listings.description: Provincetown's independently owned local magazine.

listings.name: Gibson Sotheby's International Realty
listings.description: Provincetown office of the Gibson Sotheby's real-estate brokerage, handling home and commercial sales and vacation rentals in Provincetown, Truro and Wellfleet.

photos.what: Wood End Lighthouse, Provincetown, Massachusetts, USA
photos.credit: U.S. Coast Guard (historic photograph), via Wikimedia Commons

listings.description: A small square lighthouse on the sand spit at the southwest end of Long Point. Most visitors reach it by walking the mile-long West End breakwater. It was first lit in 1872, and in 1981 it became the first lighthouse in Massachusetts to run on solar power.

history.event: First lit on November 20.
Automated; only the tower and oil house remain.
The first Massachusetts lighthouse converted to solar power.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

listings.name: Wood End Light
MacMillan Wharf
amenities: dinghy dock (4-hour free tie-up, under 16 ft)
pump-out 8 AM-3 PM daily, weather permitting
listings.description: Provincetown's town pier, reaching into the harbor from the center of Commercial Street. It is the working base for the commercial fishing fleet and the landing for the Boston ferries, whale-watch boats and harbor excursions, with the Harbormaster's office at 24 MacMillan Wharf. It is named for Arctic explorer Admiral Donald B. MacMillan, a Provincetown native.

history.event: The Old Colony Railroad Wharf is built, where ferry passengers landed and fish were loaded onto rail cars.
Construction begins on a new pier built beside and parallel to the Railroad Wharf.
The new pier is named for Admiral Donald B. MacMillan, who attends the ribbon-cutting with his wife Miriam.
Admiral MacMillan dies; the wharf keeps his name.

listings.name: Province Lands Visitor Center
listings.description: Cape Cod National Seashore's visitor center for the Outer Cape, set among the Province Lands dunes near Race Point. Inside are exhibits on the dunes, shipwrecks and people of the Province Lands, a park store, and the park film 'Standing Bold'; outside, a rooftop observation deck looks over the dunes to the Atlantic, Race Point Beach and the Old Harbor Life-Saving Station. The decks stay open year-round, weather permitting, and the Province Lands bike trail and Beech Forest Trail are close by.

history.event: Cape Cod National Seashore is established, taking in the Province Lands.
New exhibits with tactile and audio-described features open on June 13.

listings.name: Old Harbor Life-Saving Station
listings.description: A shingled 1897 life-saving station at Race Point Beach, the last intact survivor of the stations that once lined Cape Cod's outer shore. It was barged here from Chatham in 1977 and is furnished as it would have looked around 1900, with the surfboats and rescue gear the crews used on the Atlantic side. Rangers and volunteers open it on summer afternoons and stage breeches-buoy rescue drills on Thursday evenings in July and August.

history.event: Built in Chatham for the U.S. Life-Saving Service, near Chatham Harbor on Nauset Beach.
Decommissioned by the U.S. Coast Guard in July.
Sold as surplus; used as a private residence for years afterward.
Threatened by erosion, moved by barge in November to Race Point Beach, Provincetown.

listings.name: Race Point Light
listings.description: A 45-foot cast-iron lighthouse on the far northwest tip of Cape Cod, standing alone in the dunes beyond Race Point Beach. It is reached by a roughly two-mile walk over soft sand from Race Point Beach or the Hatches Harbor lot, or by four-wheel drive with a National Seashore oversand permit. The American Lighthouse Foundation keeps the station, opens the tower for free tours on summer and fall Sundays, and rents the keeper's house and whistle house for overnight stays.

history.event: First lighthouse established at Race Point, the third light on Cape Cod.
Fitted with a fourth-order Fresnel lens.
The present iron-plate tower replaces the deteriorated original.
The light is automated.
Converted to solar power; the American Lighthouse Foundation takes on care of the station.

listings.name: Long Point Light
listings.description: A square, 38-foot brick lighthouse at the very tip of Cape Cod, on the sand hook that encloses Provincetown Harbor. It stands where a fishing village of some 38 families lived until the 1850s, when residents floated many of their houses across the harbor to the West End. The tower is closed to the public; visitors reach it by a long walk over the West End breakwater and beach or by the seasonal water shuttle from town.

history.event: First Long Point light, a lantern on the keeper's house roof, is lit; a fishing settlement grows around it.
Union troops build the Long Point Battery, nicknamed 'Fort Useless' and 'Fort Ridiculous', which never sees action.
The present square brick tower replaces the eroding original.
The light is automated.
Converted to solar power, the second Massachusetts lighthouse to be.

listings.name: Provincetown Police Department
listings.description: Headquarters of the town police, a two-story, roughly 13,900-square-foot station at the corner of Route 6 and Jerome Smith Road that opened in 2024. It replaced the department's long-time quarters in a former funeral home on Shank Painter Road. For emergencies call 911; the business line handles non-emergency calls.

history.event: Construction bids come in $3.9 million over budget; the extra funding fails at April Town Meeting and at a June 18 ballot.
The building committee resumes work on a revised design in late May.
The new $17 million station is dedicated with a ribbon-cutting on March 20.

listings.name: Art's Dune Tours
listings.description: Family-run guided 4x4 tours through the Province Lands dunes, including a pass by the historic Peaked Hill dune shacks where writers and artists once lived. Offers hour-long daily tours, two-hour sunset tours with an optional clambake/bonfire, and combined dune-and-water trips.

listings.name: Provincetown Pride Center
listings.description: Home of the Provincetown Business Guild, the town's LGBTQ+ business and tourism group, with a public exhibit space on Provincetown's queer history and its role in the national gay-rights story. Opened Pride weekend 2023.

listings.name: Cape & Coast Bank
listings.description: Provincetown office of Cape & Coast Bank, the Hyannis-based community bank formerly named The Cooperative Bank of Cape Cod (rooted in 1921).

listings.name: Helltown Fitness
listings.description: Small-group strength and conditioning classes built around kettlebells, bands and bodyweight, plus yoga and running sessions, for visitors and locals.

listings.name: Gilmartin Magence LLP
listings.description: Provincetown office of a Massachusetts real-estate law firm handling residential and commercial transactions and condominium development; other offices in Boston and Newton.

listings.name: La Tanzi, Spaulding & Landreth, LLP
listings.description: Cape Cod law firm practicing real estate, business and commercial real estate, and estate planning, estate settlement and elder law.

listings.name: Provincetown Recording Studio
listings.description: Recording studio offering recording, mixing, mastering and production, plus podcast and voiceover sessions, by arrangement.

listings.name: P'Town Carts
listings.description: Rents street-legal low-speed electric carts with seatbelts, headlights and turn signals; each rental comes with a permit for the town's municipal lots.
